mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) signals robust economic growth that elevates corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring threshold conditions.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth in the prior quarter is positive but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, restrictive monetary policy compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a tightening labor market that accelerates consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days through joint labor market dynamics.
failure_condition: Joint UNRATE decline and PAYEMS increase occurs but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by housing starts (HOUST) above 1250 thousand units, strong consumer demand drives sustained corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1250 thousand units in late-cycle expansion but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates persistent inflation that triggers equity market risk aversion through higher real interest rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL increases but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.8% for two consecutive months, labor market overheating prompts aggressive central bank intervention, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 3.8% for two consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals monetary tightening coinciding with economic contraction, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through the interaction of these two series.
failure_condition: Joint FEDFUNDS increase and INDPRO decline occurs but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained stagflation regime marked by industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 and consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5%, economic stagnation and inflation pressures drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 and CPIAUCSL > 3.5% in supply-constrained stagflation but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.02.
